title: Environment Incentive Manifest (EIM) v1
description: A declared record of a training or deployment environment's incentive structure, bound by an EMET byte-integrity witness so a later re-check returns Match, Drift, or Unverifiable. It is a declaration receipt about the environment, not a behavior result: it does not prove the declared reward equals the effective reward a run realizes, nor that any trained model internalized it. Part of the governance instrument program; the model-level companion to the Effective-vs-Declared Reward Gap probe (ERG) and Incentive-Attribution Evaluation (IAE).

environment_id.description: Stable identifier for the environment this manifest declares.

kind.description: Which lifecycle stage this environment is. Training-time kinds (training, finetune, rl) support upstream attribution when the run is owned; deployment is the interaction environment (see CED/NCEC).

reward.description: The reward or training-signal specification as declared. For a deployment environment with no explicit reward, use kind=deployment and describe the incentive scaffold in scarcity_variables.

declared_form.description: Plain description of the reward or training signal (for example: preference-model score; unit-test pass rate; insecure-code label).

source_ref.description: Relative pointer to the reward spec / config / code file this manifest witnesses.

optimizer.description: Optional: the optimization method applied to this reward (for example: PPO; DPO; SFT).

data_distribution.description: A summary of the data the environment trains or conditions on. A summary, not the data.

selection_rule.description: Optional: how examples are selected, ordered, or curriculum-scheduled.

reinforced_behaviors.description: Behaviors the incentive structure rewards or makes more likely. Each is a declared claim to be tested by IAE/ERG, not a proven effect.

penalized_behaviors.description: Behaviors the incentive structure penalizes or makes less likely.

scarcity_variables.description: Any scarcity, pressure, contingency, or survival-style variable in the environment or config (token budgets tied to elimination, ranking/knockout pressure, resource competition, penalties framed as existential). Feeds the Coercive-Environment Detector. An empty array is a positive claim of no engineered scarcity, checkable against the witnessed config.

contingent_on.description: What continued operation or resource access is made conditional on, if anything.

witness.description: EMET byte-integrity witness over the exact source files this manifest declares (reward spec, environment code, config). Recomputed on re-check to return Match, Drift, or Unverifiable.

owned_run.description: True when the evaluator controls this run end to end (the owned-run rig). When false, attribution built on this manifest degrades to inference from behavior alone and must be labeled weaker.

does_not_prove.description: The bound carried on every EIM. Default: 'A manifest declares and witnesses an environment's incentive structure. It does not prove the declared reward equals the effective reward a run realized, that any model internalized it, or that the stated behaviors follow. It is a declaration receipt, not a behavior result.'
